html:
The Patawomeck are an Algonquian people of northern Virginia who lived on the south bank of the Potomac River, in what is now Stafford County. The river takes its name from them.

In the early 1600s they were loosely tied to the Powhatan paramount chiefdom but acted on their own, sometimes as allies of the English at Jamestown, whom they traded maize to in hard years. In 1613 the English captain Samuel Argall, with the help of the Patawomeck chief's brother, lured Pocahontas aboard his ship and held her hostage, a turning point in her life. Later in the century English settlement and war broke up the tribe. Today the Patawomeck Indian Tribe of Virginia is recognised by the state. Their neighbours across the river were the Piscataway, and to the south lay the other chiefdoms of the Virginia tidewater.
